claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have one child, Alex, who's 21 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to ask some questions about Alex to determine eligibility.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just to confirm a few more details:

Are you responsible for Alex - meaning, does Alex live with you or do you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit would pay towards their upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me. I do help out with some money for their expenses - I give them about £20 a week to help with bits and pieces.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just to clarify - do you know approximately how much Child Benefit pays per week for one child? This will help me determine if your contribution meets the threshold required for eligibility.

Also, can you confirm whether you are the main person responsible for Alex, or is there someone else (such as Alex's other parent) who provides more support or has Alex living with them?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
I'm not entirely sure what the exact Child Benefit amount is - could you tell me? 

As for who's responsible, Alex lives with their other parent, not with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Child Benefit is currently £25.60 per week for the eldest or only child (or £16.95 per week for additional children).

Since you mentioned you contribute about £20 per week, which is less than the £25.60 Child Benefit amount, and Alex lives with their other parent, I have a few more questions:

Does Alex's other parent claim Child Benefit for Alex, or are they responsible for Alex's main upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex's other parent is the one who lives with them and takes care of most of their needs day-to-day.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

**Age Limit:** Child Benefit generally stops when a child turns 16. It can continue until they turn 20 (or sometimes until the end of their course) if they remain in approved education or training. Since Alex is 21 and not in education or training, they are over the age limit for Child Benefit.

**Responsibility Test:** Even if the age requirement were met, you would also need to meet the "responsibility" test. This means either having the child live with you, or contributing at least the same amount as Child Benefit pays (£25.60 per week for an eldest/only child) towards their upkeep. Since you contribute approximately £20 per week, which is less than £25.60, and Alex lives with their other parent who provides the main day-to-day care, you wouldn't meet this requirement either.

If you have any other questions or if your circumstances change in the future, please don't hesitate to ask.
